deviations.what: Main-agent integration after t14 and t16: (1) the per-test reset in tests/conftest.py now drops any public index a test created, so an HNSW index for a new (model, strategy) pair no longer leaks into later tests; (2) search._ann completes a group of exactly tied chunks the pool LIMIT cut (fetch limit+1; on a tie at the edge, score that distance exactly), so ties break on (owner, chunk_no) and every k is a prefix of a larger k
deviations.reason: both caused intermittent full-suite failures; the tie case is real on live, where many repo docs are byte-identical (.devague/current), and SQLite's exhaustive scan always ordered ties the same way

deviations.what: Ship 0.20.1 before the cutover: the copy knows 0.19.8's vector_log (the vector cache's change log, derived state Postgres has no use for) and skips it, naming it and its row count in the report; the source fixture gains vector_log and its triggers so the tests use the real 0.19.8 schema. t19 runs on 0.20.1.
deviations.reason: The t18 drill's copy of the real live library.db refused it (unknown vector_log); the cutover cannot run on 0.20.0.

deviations.what: 0.20.1 also changes backup restore: it leaves the dump's EXTENSION and COMMENT ON EXTENSION entries out (via a filtered pg_restore --use-list), requires the target to already have the vector extension (created by the superuser, as the init script does), and refuses up front with that remediation when it is missing. backup.md says how to make the restore target.
deviations.reason: The t18 drill's restore as the app role failed on the dump's extension entries; a live restore would fail the same way.

deviations.what: Correction to d16's mechanism: restore passes pg_restore --no-comments instead of a filtered --use-list. The rest of d16 stands (vector extension required up front, refused with the superuser remediation, backup.md updated).
deviations.reason: Smaller than the TOC filter d16 named: the dump's only COMMENT is the extension's, and its CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS is a no-op for a non-owner once the extension exists; a --use-list file would also not reach the test suite's docker-exec pg_restore wrapper.

deviations.what: 0.20.1 also narrows d13's tie completion to chunks whose text equals a tied chunk's text before scoring them, instead of rescoring the whole corpus. Identical vectors come from identical text under one (model, strategy); a different-text chunk at exactly the same float distance is no longer pulled in, which the code comment states.
deviations.reason: Measured on the t18 scratch copy of live data: combined search p95 546 ms against the < 500 ms success signal; the slow statement (about 260 ms, 5 of 40 queries) is d13's tie completion, which scores all 62,591 repo-doc vectors whenever the pool edge falls in a group of identical vectors (the same file pushed from many repos). Narrowing by chunk text first costs about 11 ms.

deviations.what: Corrects d18 and d17. Tie completion finds identical vectors by vec_hash, an indexed md5 of each vector added by migration 0003 (schema version 3), not by chunk text, so it is exact again and still scores only the tie group. Restore leaves out only the dump's COMMENT ON EXTENSION vector entry, via a filtered pg_restore --use-list (d16's original mechanism), and keeps every other comment. Restore also refuses a target whose vector extension is outside public, or whose collation is not C.
deviations.reason: /code-review medium of PR #50: text equality is only a proxy for the tie condition (the restored original test, distinct texts with identical vectors, fails under it), and --no-comments would silently drop every future table or column comment on restore.

deviations.what: Change s21's third case: a trailing stopword the english config drops is no longer required to match as a simple prefix; the other words must still match, and ranking is unchanged. Ship as 0.20.2, deploy with deploy restart, rerun t20.
deviations.reason: t20 on live: newspapers with rerank average 0.917 ID recall@5 against the >= 0.95 target (set 6: 0.75, was 1.0 on 0.19.8; stable over 3 runs). Question 103 ('...JetPack 7.0 ship with?') ends in a stopword; s21 makes that last word match only as a prefix of a stored lexeme or title word, and the english tsv never stores the stopword itself, so item 81 (which has every content word) is filtered out of the full-text owners. FTS5 had no stopwords and matched the word itself. Without the requirement item 81 ranks first. 10 of the 112 eval questions end in a stopword.

deviations.what: Correction to d20's mechanism: the trailing stopword is still required, but it now also matches as a word start in the raw body (body ~* '\mwith'), as FTS5 matched the word itself; evaluated only on rows the english query already matched. Ships as 0.20.2.
deviations.reason: Dropping the trailing-stopword requirement (d20's mechanism) would break FTS5 parity the suite pins: 'road the' must not match 'Road map', which has no 'the'. A word-start regex over the raw body keeps it: measured on live, the 10 stopword-ending eval questions cost at most 6 ms (mean 1.0 -> 1.9 ms), and question 103's full-text owners go from 4 to 9, item 81 included.

deviations.what: Supersedes d21's mechanism: migration 0004 (schema version 4) adds simple_tsv, a GIN-indexed 'simple' tsvector of each body (stopwords kept), and the trailing stopword is checked as a prefix there (the same tsquery as the title and lexeme checks), not by a regex. Measured on live's text: about 49 MB, 3 s to build.
deviations.reason: /code-review medium of PR #51: the d21 regex was unindexed (it scans whole multi-MB book bodies on a miss), and it was built from a different piece than the tsquery's last word, so a query ending in a lone '?' ('road the ?') made it a bare \m that matched every body; the new parametrized test reproduced both.

deviations.reason: r2 measured on live 0.20.2 (40 questions, HNSW top-10 vs exact): items exact at 40/40 under operator and public-only filters; repo docs (62.6k chunks, many near-duplicates) 0.853 at ef_search 100, misses near-ties (10th distance at most 0.0066 farther). ef_search 200: 0.922 (+1 ms); 400: 0.953 (+5 ms); 1000: 1.000 (+129 ms).

deltas.behavior_text: migrate sqlite-to-postgres reads past 0.19.8's vector_log (the vector cache's change log) and names it with its row count in the report, instead of refusing the live library.db

backup restore runs as the least-privilege app role: it leaves out only the dump's COMMENT ON EXTENSION vector entry, and refuses a target without the vector extension in public or without the C collation
completing an exact tie at the HNSW pool's edge looks the identical vectors up by vec_hash (migration 0003, indexed), so only the tie group is scored, not the whole corpus

a query's trailing stopword matches as a prefix in the body's simple_tsv (migration 0004), so a question ending in 'with?' finds a document that says 'with', as FTS5 did; a document with no word starting with it still does not match
HNSW search breadth is per corpus: ef_search 100 for items, 400 for repo docs
